target_customer: Medical practices and digital health companies that pay for practice management and billing software
problem: Medical billing is opaque and slow for practices and patients, with eligibility checks, claims and patient payments handled by disconnected tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS and billing services for healthcare practices
product_category: Healthcare practice management and revenue cycle software

founders.name: Nick Shelly
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. The company site says it was founded by former National Security Agency and industry veterans without naming people.

founders.name: Jacinda Shelly
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. The YC description says the team includes the CTO of Doctor on Demand without naming who. Aggregator profiles say Jacinda was CTO there, unverified.

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires integrations with EHRs, payer eligibility and claims systems, which are standard but fiddly engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Billing software had many vendors and integrations were copyable, but practices are slow to switch once billing runs through a platform.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response was found. The company site compares itself to unnamed legacy EHRs and other RCM vendors.

market_need_then: The YC description cites a need for price transparency for patients and providers and says the customers include startups that raised over 1 billion dollars. No dated third party demand data was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Healthcare software for innovators, with security credentials such as HIPAA and SOC 2 Type 2 emphasized

brand_strength.rationale: Only the company site and YC page were found. Search results mix it up with similarly named companies such as Aperio Health and Ampero Health.

outcome_analysis: Apero Health remains active with about 24 people and a broader product (scheduling, visit notes, revenue cycle, patient billing, prescriptions). Public funding information is thin, so the capital story cannot be judged. The company site highlights SOC 2 Type 2 and HIPAA readiness. With no verified rounds or outcome events, the story is unresolved rather than a success or failure.
notes: Funding figures are unverified and all from aggregators: Dealroom 150K and 125K seeds, Persana 150K, CB Insights about 800K over five rounds with a 400K convertible note on 2022-07-27, Seedtable (via Crunchbase) an August 2019 seed from Y Combinator, Soma Capital and angels including Paul Buchheit. The YC description names angels Paul Buchheit and founders of Doctor on Demand, Gusto and Reddit but gives no amounts. A name origin from the French aperitif appears on one aggregator profile only, so it is not recorded. Aggregator competitor names (RXNT, PracticeSuite, CureMD) are undated and not listed. Education: the YC description says the founding team are Stanford CS and Berkeley grads, with no assignment to individuals. No layoffs, acquisition or shutdown found. Completeness pass: the August 2019 seed is recorded from Seedtable (investors YC, Soma Capital and angels incl. Paul Buchheit) with the 150K amount from Dealroom and Persana; Persana dates it 2019-09-19. The 400K convertible note of 2022-07-27 rests on CB Insights alone, which also states about 800K over five rounds and an outlier 25M entry that is not used. Amounts conflict across databases, so unverified.
